extracted.intended_audience: public water system operators (community and nontransient noncommunity), water utility managers, and State drinking water regulators
extracted.subtask_description: EPA regulatory requirements for monitoring, compliance calculations, reporting, and recordkeeping for Stage 2 Disinfection Byproducts (TTHM and HAA5) and source-water Cryptosporidium monitoring, including schedules, sampling locations, analytical methods, and actions triggered by exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring location selection protocol (subpart V / §141.605 order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of priority for identifying subpart V monitoring locations (alternating high TTHM and HAA5 LRAA and using existing subpart L average residence time/maximum residence time locations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit itemized selection sequence: (1) Location with the highest TTHM LRAA not previously selected as a subpart V monitoring location; (2) Location with the highest HAA5 LRAA not previously selected; (3) Existing subpart L average residence time compliance monitoring location with the highest HAA5 LRAA not previously selected; (4) Location with the highest TTHM LRAA not previously selected; (5) Location with the highest TTHM LRAA not previously selected; (6) Location with the highest HAA5 LRAA not previously selected; (7) Existing subpart L average residence time compliance monitoring location with the highest TTHM LRAA not previously selected; (8) Location with the highest HAA5 LRAA not previously selected. You may recommend alternate locations with rationale; State approval required to use alternates. Recommended schedule must include monitoring during the peak historical month for TTHM and HAA5 unless State approves another month.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Subpart V requirements (§141.620)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart V establishes monitoring and other requirements for achieving compliance with maximum contaminant levels based on locational running annual averages (LRAA) for TTHM and HAA5 and for MRDLs for chlorine and chloramine for certain consecutive systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are national primary drinking water regulations; they apply to community water systems and nontransient noncommunity water systems that use a primary or residual disinfectant other than ultraviolet light or deliver water treated with such disinfectant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance schedule by system population (§141.620(c) table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must comply with subpart V monitoring by specified dates based on system population and system type (not part of combined distribution vs combined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: systems serving ≥100,000 must comply by April 1, 2012; 50,000–99,999 by Oct 1, 2012; 10,000–49,999 by Oct 1, 2013; <10,000 by Oct 1, 2013 if no Cryptosporidium monitoring is required under §141.701(a)(4) or Oct 1, 2014 if Cryptosporidium monitoring is required. Consecutive or wholesale systems comply at the same time as the system with the earliest compliance date in the combined distribution system. State may grant up to an additional 24 months for compliance with MCLs and OELs if capital improvements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring start timing rules (§141.620(c)(6)-(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: When to begin monitoring depending on monitoring frequency (quarterly vs less-than-quarterly) and IDSE/subpart V monitoring plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required to conduct quarterly monitoring, begin in the first full calendar quarter that includes the compliance date. If monitoring less frequently than quarterly, begin in the calendar month recommended in the IDSE report or monitoring plan no later than 12 months after the compliance date. If quarterly, make compliance calculations at end of fourth calendar quarter following compliance date and at end of each subsequent quarter (or earlier if LRAA based on fewer than four quarters would cause MCL exceedance regardless of subsequent results). If less frequent, begin compliance calculations with the first compliance sample taken after the compliance date.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion for combined distribution membership (§141.620(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: State may determine that certain consecutive or wholesale systems are not included in a combined distribution system based on specific factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include receiving water from a wholesale system only on emergency basis or receiving only a small percentage and small volume of water; similarly for wholesale systems delivering to consecutive systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: LRAA calculation and quarterly monitoring rules (§141.620(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to monitor quarterly must calculate LRAAs for TTHM and HAA5 using monitoring results collected under this subpart and determine that each LRAA does not exceed the MCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fail to complete four consecutive quarters, calculate compliance based on average of available data from most recent four quarters. If more than one sample per quarter at a monitoring location, average all samples taken in the quarter at that location to determine quarterly average to be used in LRAA calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring rules for yearly or less frequent sampling (§141.620(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems required to monitor yearly or less frequently, each sample must be less than the MCL to be in compliance; if any sample exceeds the MCL, §141.625 applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no sample exceeds MCL, the sample result for each monitoring location is considered the LRAA for that location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring violation definition for failure to monitor (§141.620(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to monitor is a violation for each quarter that a monitoring result would be used in calculating an LRAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies irrespective of whether measured values exceed MCLs; missing data that would figure into LRAA constitutes violation for those quarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of monitoring locations and monitoring frequency by source and population (§141.621(a)(2) & footnotes)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must monitor at no fewer than the number of locations identified in the monitoring frequency/location table based on source water type and population size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table summarizes distribution system monitoring location totals and monitoring frequency. Key examples: Subpart H surface water: <500: per year, 2 locations; 500–3,300: per quarter, 2 locations; 10,000–49,999: per quarter, 4 locations; ≥5,000,000: per quarter, 20 locations. Ground water: <500 per year 2 locations; ≥500,000 per quarter 8 locations. Footnotes: All systems must monitor during month of highest DBP concentrations. Systems on quarterly monitoring must take dual sample sets every 90 days at each monitoring location except certain small subpart H systems. Ground water systems on annual monitoring must take dual sample sets at each monitoring location for some sizes. Small-system special-case rules for number and type of samples are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin monitoring at IDSE-recommended locations/months (§141.621(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submitted an IDSE report, begin monitoring at locations and months recommended in that report following schedule in §141.620(c), unless State requires other or additional locations after review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submitted 40/30 certification or qualified for very small system waiver or are NTN community serving <10,000, monitor at locations/dates in monitoring plan per §141.132(f), updated as required by §141.622.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undisinfected systems beginning to use disinfectant must consult State (§141.621(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: An undisinfected system that begins using a disinfectant other than UV after the IDSE dates must consult the State to identify compliance monitoring locations and develop a monitoring plan under §141.622 including those locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State consultation required to identify appropriate compliance monitoring locations for subpart V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical methods and laboratory certification (§141.621(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must use an approved method listed in §141.131 for TTHM and HAA5 analyses in this subpart, and analyses must be conducted by laboratories certified by EPA or the State as specified in §141.131.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only approved analytical methods and certified laboratories are acceptable for compliance monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart V monitoring plan required elements (§141.622(a)(1)(i)-(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must develop and implement a monitoring plan to be kept on file for State and public review; the plan must contain monitoring locations, monitoring dates, compliance calculation procedures, and monitoring plans for other systems in combined distribution if State reduced monitoring under §142.16(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must be complete no later than the date you conduct initial monitoring under this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of additional monitoring locations when no IDSE or insufficient subpart L locations (§141.622(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If not required to submit IDSE and insufficient subpart L monitoring locations to identify required number of subpart V compliance locations, you must identify additional locations by alternating selection of locations representing high TTHM and high HAA5 levels until required number identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must provide rationale for identifying locations as high TTHM or HAA5. If you have more subpart L locations than required, identify which locations you will use for subpart V compliance monitoring by alternating selection of high TTHM and high HAA5 locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring plan submission and revisions (§141.622(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart H systems serving >3,300 must submit a copy of monitoring plan to State prior to initial monitoring unless IDSE report already contains required info. Monitoring plans may be revised to reflect changes in treatment, distribution operations/layout, or other factors affecting DBP formation, after consultation with State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you change monitoring locations, replace existing compliance locations with the lowest LRAA with new locations expected to have high TTHM or HAA5. State may require modifications; for subpart H >3,300, submit modified plan to State prior to compliance with revised plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for reduced monitoring (§141.623(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: You may reduce monitoring to the level specified if the LRAA is ≤0.040 mg/L for TTHM and ≤0.030 mg/L for HAA5 at all monitoring locations, and source water annual average TOC before treatment ≤4.0 mg/L at each treatment plant treating surface water or GWUDI, based on monitoring under §141.132(b)(1)(iii) or §141.132(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may only use data collected under this subpart or subpart L to qualify for reduced monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced monitoring frequency/location table (§141.623(a) table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table specifies reduced monitoring frequency and number/type of samples by source water type and population size when qualifying for reduced monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Subpart H 500–3,300: per year — 1 TTHM and 1 HAA5 sample (one at location/quarter with highest single measurement each); 3,301–9,999: per year — 2 dual sample sets; 10,000–49,999: per quarter — 2 dual sample sets at locations with highest TTHM and HAA5 LRAAs. Ground water categories have analogous reduced frequencies and sample sets. Footnote: Systems on quarterly monitoring must take dual sample sets every 90 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain on reduced monitoring conditions (§141.623(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: You may remain on reduced monitoring as long as TTHM LRAA ≤0.040 mg/L and HAA5 LRAA ≤0.030 mg/L at each monitoring location (for quarterly reduced monitoring) OR each TTHM sample ≤0.060 mg/L and each HAA5 sample ≤0.045 mg/L (for annual or less frequent monitoring), and source water annual average TOC ≤4.0 mg/L at each treatment plant treating surface water or GWUDI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring data used to qualify must be from subpart V or L as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions requiring resumption of routine or increased monitoring (§141.623(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the LRAA based on quarterly monitoring at any location exceeds either 0.040 mg/L TTHM or 0.030 mg/L HAA5, or if the annual (or less frequent) sample at any location exceeds either 0.060 mg/L TTHM or 0.045 mg/L HAA5, or source water annual average TOC before treatment >4.0 mg/L at any treatment plant treating surface water or GWUDI, you must resume routine monitoring or begin increased monitoring if §141.625 applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may return system to routine monitoring at State's discretion (§141.623(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consecutive systems chlorine/chloramine monitoring and compliance (§141.624)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consecutive systems that do not add a disinfectant but deliver water treated with a primary or residual disinfectant other than UV must comply with analytical and monitoring requirements for chlorine and chloramines in §§141.131(c) and 141.132(c)(1) and compliance requirements in §141.133(c)(1) beginning April 1, 2009 (unless required earlier by State), and report results under §141.134(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to consecutive systems delivering disinfected water even if they do not add disinfectant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased monitoring triggers (§141.625(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If required to monitor annually or less frequently, you must increase monitoring to dual sample sets once per quarter (every 90 days) at all locations if any TTHM sample >0.080 mg/L or any HAA5 sample >0.060 mg/L at any location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trigger applies to previously lower-frequency monitoring schedules and forces quarterly dual-sample increased monitoring across locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCL violation definition for LRAA (§141.625(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: You are in violation of the MCL when the LRAA exceeds the subpart V MCLs, calculated based on four consecutive quarters of monitoring (or based on fewer than four quarters if the MCL would be exceeded regardless of subsequent results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also reiterates that failure to monitor is a monitoring violation for each quarter a monitoring result would be used in calculating an LRAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return to routine monitoring after increased monitoring (§141.625(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: You may return to routine monitoring once you have conducted increased monitoring for at least four consecutive quarters and the LRAA for every monitoring location is ≤0.060 mg/L for TTHM and ≤0.045 mg/L for HAA5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides numeric thresholds for return to routine monitoring after increased monitoring period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational evaluation level (OEL) calculation (§141.626(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: You have exceeded the operational evaluation level at a monitoring location where (sum of two previous quarters' result + twice the current quarter's result)/4 > 0.080 mg/L for TTHM OR > 0.060 mg/L for HAA5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEL is a weighted-average calculation that emphasizes the current quarter (current quarter counted twice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational evaluation actions and reporting (§141.626(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If you exceed the OEL you must conduct an operational evaluation and submit a written report to the State no later than 90 days after being notified of the analytical result that causes the exceedance; the report must be available to the public upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational evaluation must examine system treatment and distribution operational practices (storage tank operations, excess storage capacity, distribution flushing, changes in sources or source water quality, treatment changes/problems) and identify steps to minimize future exceedances. You may request State approval to limit scope of evaluation; such request does not extend the 90-day report deadline; State must approve limited scope in writing and you must keep approval with the completed report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remaining on reduced monitoring based on subpart L results (§141.627)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may remain on reduced monitoring after the dates identified in §141.620(c) only if you qualify for a 40/30 certification under §141.603 or have a very small system waiver under §141.604, meet reduced monitoring criteria in §141.623(a), and do not change or add monitoring locations from those used for subpart L compliance monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If monitoring locations under this subpart differ from subpart L locations, you may not remain on reduced monitoring after the compliance dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remaining on increased monitoring based on subpart L results (§141.628)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you were on increased monitoring under §141.132(b)(1), you must remain on increased monitoring until you qualify to return to routine monitoring under §141.625(c). You must conduct increased monitoring under §141.625 at the monitoring locations in the monitoring plan beginning at the date in §141.620(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity of increased monitoring status derived from earlier subpart L determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for monitoring locations (§141.629(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must report specified information for each monitoring location to the State within 10 days of the end of any quarter in which monitoring is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report: (i) number of samples taken during the last quarter; (ii) date and results of each sample taken during the last quarter; (iii) arithmetic average of quarterly results for the last four quarters for each monitoring location (LRAA), beginning at the end of the fourth calendar quarter that follows the compliance date and at the end of each subsequent quarter (or sooner if LRAA based on fewer than four quarters would cause MCL exceedance); (iv) whether, based on §141.64(b)(2) and this subpart, the MCL was violated at any monitoring location; (v) any OELs exceeded during the quarter and, if so, the location and date, and the calculated TTHM and HAA5 levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water TOC reporting for subpart H reduced monitoring applicants (§141.629(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a subpart H system seeking to qualify for or remain on reduced TTHM/HAA5 monitoring, you must report source water TOC information for each treatment plant treating surface water or GWUDI within 10 days of the end of any quarter in which monitoring is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report: (i) number of source water TOC samples taken each month during last quarter; (ii) date and result of each sample; (iii) quarterly average of monthly samples or result of quarterly sample; (iv) running annual average (RAA) of quarterly averages from past four quarters; (v) whether RAA exceeded 4.0 mg/L.

rubrics_metrics.name: State may perform calculations in lieu of system reporting (§141.629(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may choose to perform calculations and determine whether the MCL was exceeded or the system is eligible for reduced monitoring instead of having the system report that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State discretion available to reduce reporting burden; systems must still submit sample data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping retention (§141.629(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must retain any subpart V monitoring plans and subpart V monitoring results as required by §141.33.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §141.33 retention requirements for records that demonstrate compliance and support State/EPA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart W applicability and general requirements (§141.700)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart W establishes enhanced treatment (treatment technique) requirements for Cryptosporidium for all subpart H systems (surface water and GWUDI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wholesale systems must comply based on population of largest system in combined distribution; filtered system requirements apply even if filtration not currently operated; unfiltered system requirements apply only to unfiltered systems that timely met and continue to meet filtration avoidance criteria in subparts H, P, and T.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial source water monitoring requirements (Subpart W §141.701(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must conduct an initial round of source water monitoring on the schedule in §141.701(c) unless meeting monitoring exemptions; parameters/frequencies vary by system type/size (Cryptosporidium, E. coli, turbidity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key frequency rules: filtered systems serving ≥10,000: sample source water for Cryptosporidium, E. coli, and turbidity at least monthly for 24 months; unfiltered systems ≥10,000: sample for Cryptosporidium at least monthly for 24 months; filtered systems <10,000: E. coli at least once every two weeks for 12 months (or may avoid if notifying State to monitor for Cryptosporidium instead); filtered systems <10,000 may need Cryptosporidium sampling twice per month for 12 months or monthly for 24 months based on E. coli trigger levels or if not conducting E. coli monitoring; unfiltered systems <10,000: Cryptosporidium at least twice per month for 12 months or monthly for 24 months. Systems may sample more frequently if evenly spaced throughout monitoring period. GWUDI systems follow nearest surface water E. coli triggers; State may approve indicator alternatives or different trigger levels in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second round of source water monitoring (§141.701(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must conduct a second round of source water monitoring that meets the same requirements for parameters, frequency, and duration described for the initial round, unless they meet monitoring exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second round must be conducted on schedule in §141.701(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water monitoring schedule by system size (§141.701(c) table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start dates for first and second rounds of monitoring are specified by system population brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: systems serving at least 100,000: begin first round Oct 1, 2006 and second round Apr 1, 2015. 50,000–99,999: first Apr 1, 2007 second Oct 1, 2015. 10,000–49,999: first Apr 1, 2008 second Oct 1, 2016. Fewer than 10,000 with E. coli monitoring: first Oct 1, 2008 second Oct 1, 2017. Fewer than 10,000 with Cryptosporidium monitoring: first Apr 1, 2010 second Apr 1, 2019.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring avoidance by providing treatment instead (§141.701(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Filtered systems need not conduct source water monitoring if they will provide at least 5.5-log Cryptosporidium treatment (equivalent to Bin 4); unfiltered systems need not monitor if they will provide at least 3-log Cryptosporidium inactivation equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If choosing treatment instead of monitoring, notify State in writing no later than date system otherwise required to submit sampling schedule. Systems may stop sampling after initiating monitoring if they notify State in writing that they will provide required treatment. Systems must install and operate technologies to provide required treatment by applicable treatment compliance date in §141.713.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-year plant operation modifications (§141.701(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems with plants that operate only part of the year must conduct monitoring during months plant operates, with special rules for plants operating less than six months per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plants operating <6 months per year that monitor for Cryptosporidium must collect at least six Cryptosporidium samples per year during each of two years of monitoring; samples must be evenly spaced throughout operation period. State may specify another monitoring period based on plant practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: New sources monitoring and bin classification timing (§141.701(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A system that begins using a new surface water or GWUDI source after required monitoring start date must monitor the new source on a State-approved schedule meeting subpart requirements and must meet bin classification and treatment requirements on a State-approved schedule; second round monitoring must begin no later than 6 years following initial bin classification or determination of mean Cryptosporidium level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies also to systems that begin operation after the monitoring start date applicable to their size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to collect required source water sample is monitoring violation (§141.701(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to collect any source water sample required under the section in accordance with sampling schedule, location, analytical method, approved laboratory, and reporting requirements is a monitoring violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance triggers monitoring violation enforcement; follow sampling, lab, reporting protocols to avoid violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandfathering prior monitoring data (§141.701(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems may use prior monitoring data to meet initial source water monitoring requirements if data meet §141.707 requirements; grandfathered data may substitute for an equivalent number of months at end of monitoring period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All grandfathered data submitted must meet criteria in §141.707 (quality, representativeness, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling schedule submission deadlines and methods (§141.702(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to conduct source water monitoring must submit a sampling schedule specifying calendar dates when each required sample will be collected, no later than 3 months prior to applicable start date for each round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems serving ≥10,000 must submit initial-round sampling schedule electronically to https://intranet.epa.gov/lt2/ (or approved alternative if unable). Systems serving <10,000 submit to State. Second round schedules submitted to State. If EPA/State does not respond, system must sample at reported schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling date windows and replacement-sample timing (§141.702(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must collect samples within two days before or two days after scheduled date (5-day window) unless exceptional conditions apply; if unable to report valid analytical result due to equipment failure, lost/damaged sample, method QC failure, or lab failure, system must collect replacement sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sample must be collected no later than 21 days after receiving information that a valid analytical result cannot be reported unless infeasible or State approves alternative resampling date. System must submit explanation for delayed sampling date to State concurrent with shipment of sample to lab. Extreme dangerous conditions allow sampling as close as feasible or State-approved alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missed-sample schedule revision requirement (§141.702(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that fail to meet sampling date-window criteria must revise sampling schedules to add dates for collecting all missed samples and submit revised schedule to State for approval prior to collecting missed samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive schedule revision and State approval required before collecting replacements to demonstrate compliance planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling location rules (§141.703(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must collect source water samples for each plant that treats a surface water or GWUDI source. Where multiple plants draw from the same influent, State may approve one set of monitoring results to satisfy requirements for all plants. Samples must be collected prior to chemical treatment unless State approves after-treatment sampling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State approval required in writing to sample after chemical treatment; otherwise pre-chemical treatment sampling is mandatory to characterize source water.
